chapter: Nola band, day job and nightclub work
title: Nine-to-four nightclub job on Iberville and being fired for napping
summary: Playing at Johnny Cialina's place from nine to four after day work lasted six months, until the band manager got him fired for napping.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You never did like play every night then?

Yeah, I'll tell you one place now. I can't call, I could call the name of the man, ran the place. The name was Johnny C. Olena. He ran the place on Iberville between Wyvern and Royal. I used to have to go to work there at nine o'clock at night, work till four in the morning, and then try to work till the day.
That must have lasted too long. Well I'll tell you what happened, it lasted about six months. Oh yeah.

I'll tell you what made it a little better for me. I rented a room in town, see, close to where the day work was. And when I'd knock off from playing music at night, go to this room and I'd sleep the, excuse me, tell it was time to go to work today. It lasted about six months. Must have been really hard.

Well what I used to do every night, tell you the truth, that's how I lost the job too. I'd get down off the bandstand about twelve o'clock, I'd go to the man's restroom, wash my face up and sit around there and take a nap. And the band manager, he got mad about that, and he got me fired. But I'm kind of glad he got me fired. I'll get some of that off there. I'll call his name, you might know him. His name is Eric Begaard. Oh yeah.
Yeah, yeah. He had a job in charge.
You were going into missions and taking a nap.
